question: How much will Crude Oil Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 9 - Nov 20)

calls.reasoning: Random-walk zero-drift anchor for a 2-week CL-ES spread. Oil is in a high-vol geopolitical regime (OVX ~58, WTI fell ~13% last week to $90.83 on Iran diplomacy hopes, tanker attacks ongoing), ES vol elevated (VIX ~25). Diff SD ~10.5-14pp. Slight negative median shift for a possible Yahoo CL=F front-month roll (Dec contract expires ~Nov 20) in a backwardated curve. Fat tails both ways: war resumption -> oil spike above +25 (~6%); peace deal/Hormuz normalization -> oil collapse below -25 (~4%). No human market found on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold.

- Base rate: zero-drift random walk for 2-week spread; historical biweekly diff sd in calm regimes ~5-6pp, in 2022/2026-crisis regimes ~10-15pp.
- Escape mechanisms: war resumption/Hormuz disruption (CL +25%+), comprehensive deal (CL -25%+).

calls.reasoning: Zero-drift random walk for the 2-week CL-ES spread, with dispersion dominated by crude vol (OVX ~58) in an Iran war/diplomacy regime. WTI fell 13% last week to $90.83 (P0); the catalysts run both ways: a US-Iran deal (oil down, stocks up) vs Hormuz escalation (oil spike, stocks down). Median shifted about -0.7pp for a ~50% chance that Yahoo CL=F rolls from the expiring Dec contract (last trade Nov 20) to Jan in a ~2% backwardated curve. Both tails beyond ±25 are priced. calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the facts (P0 prices, OVX ~58, VIX ~25, no market). The only factual question is whether Yahoo CL=F rolls to Jan by the Nov 20 close. CLZ26 last trade is Nov 20 (3 business days before Wed Nov 25). Yahoo historically shows the expiring contract until at least the day before expiry (e.g., the Apr 20 2020 print), so a roll on expiry day itself is about a coin flip. I couldn't verify it without web access, so it carries ~-1pp of expected bias and sets the median at -0.7. The tail widths are a judgment call: a normal distribution with SD ~11 gives ~1.5% beyond each bound, and the bimodal war/peace risk fattens that, so I priced ~3.5% low and ~4.5% high (upside spikes come faster in supply shocks). I carried forward the dispersion from Runs 1/3.
